title: CRLR/445/2019 of BIMLA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 578 of 2019
Sunil Negi ..........Revisionist
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand ........ Respondent

Present : Ms. Nidhi Thapa, Advocate holding brief of Mr. Gaurav Singh,
Advocate for the revisionist.
 Mr. Lalit Miglani, A.G.A. for the State.
 Mr. Shariq Khurshid, Advocate for the informant.

With
Criminal Revision No. 445 of 2019
Smt. Bimla and others ..........Revisionists
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand ........ Respondent

Present : Ms. Nidhi Thapa, Advocate holding brief of Mr. Gaurav Singh,
Advocate for the revisionist.
 Mr. Lalit Miglani, A.G.A. for the State.
 Mr. Shariq Khurshid, Advocate for the informant.
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 A common question of law arises in these
petitions; therefore, they are being decided by this
common judgment.

2
2. The challenge in this revision is made to the
following:-
 (i) Judgment and order dated
06.02.2012, passed in Criminal Case
No.2435 of 2006, State Vs. Sunil Negi
and others, by the court of Chief
Judicial Magistrate, Haridwar,
District Haridwar (for short, "the
case"). By it, the revisionists have
been convicted under Sections 498A,
323, 504, 506 IPC and Sections 3/4
of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961
(for short, "the Act") and sentenced as
hereunder:-
 (a) Under Section 498A IPC -
three months' imprisonment
and a fine of `2,000/ each. In
default of payment of fine,
imprisonment for a further
period of three months.
 (b) Under Section 323 IPC - six
months' imprisonment and a
fine of `500/- each one. In

3
default of payment of fine,
imprisonment for a further
period of five days.
 (c) Under Section 504 IPC, six
months' imprisonment and a
fine of `500/- each. In default
of payment of fine,
imprisonment for a further
period of five days and;
 (d) Under Section 506 IPC, one
year imprisonment and a fine
of `1,000/- each. In default of
payment of fine, imprisonment
for a further period of one
month.
 (e) Under Section 3/4 of the Act,
three years' imprisonment and
a fine of `2,000/- each. In
default of payment of fine,
imprisonment for a further
period of three months.

4
 (ii) Judgment and order dated
02.07.2019, passed in Criminal
Appeal No.26of 2012, Sunil Negi and
others vs. State of Uttarakhand, by
the court of 4th Additional Sessions
Judge, Haridwar, District Haridwar
(for short, "the appeal"). By it, the
appeal filed by the revisionists has
been dismissed and the judgment and
order passed in the case has been
affirmed.
3. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
4. Now Compounding Application (IA) Nos.3022 of
2022 and 2093 of 2022 have been filed by the revisionists
on the ground that the parties have settled the dispute.
The case has its origin on an FIR lodged by the informant
Smt. Sarojini Devi (for short, "the informant") with the
averment that she and the revisionist Sunil Negi were
married on 11.05.2003, but after marriage the informant
was harassed and tortured in connection with additional
demand of dowry; she was beaten up. Based on this
report, investigation was carried out and charge-sheet

5
was submitted against the revisionist, in which, the
conviction and sentence was recorded and upheld in the
appeal.
5. The joint compounding applications have been
filed in both the cases by the revisionists and the
informant.
6. It is a settled law that under certain
circumstances even after conviction, matter may be
decided on the basis of amicable settlement between the
parties.
7. The revisionists Smt. Bimla, Smt. Hema,
Dinesh Negi and Sunil Negi are present in the Court, as
identified by Ms. Nidhi Thapa, Advocate for the
revisionists and the informant Smt. Sarojini Devi, as
identified by Mr. Shariq Khurshid, Advocate for the
informant. They have stated that they have settled the
dispute amicably.
8. On being asked, the informant would tell that
she has settled the dispute with the revisionists and she
does not want to proceed with the case.

6
9. Having considered the nature of the offence
and the other attending factors, this Court is of the view
that the criminal revision may be decided in terms of the
compromise between the parties. Accordingly, the petition
deserves to be allowed.
10. Accordingly, the instant criminal revision is
allowed. The judgment and order dated 06.02.2012
passed in the case and the order dated 02.07.2019,
passed in the appeal, are hereby quashed. The
revisionists are acquitted of the charge under Sections
Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and Sections 3/4 of the
of the Act.
11. Compounding Application (IA) Nos.3022 of
2022 and 2093 of 2022, stand disposed of accordingly.
12. Let a copy of this order along with the record be
sent to the court concerned.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 09.11.2022
Sanjay
